headline: ChatGPT-6 Astra cracks 1941 Enigma-coded message in two days
summary: The LLM independently developed software to decipher an 85-year-old German Army Enigma transmission, a task that would take human researchers weeks or months.
details: A German Army Enigma transmission from July 10, 1941, known as the MVUEH message, has been cracked by GPT-Astra in just two days. This message, sent at the height of Nazi military power in WWII, had remained uncracked since it was shared online in 2005.

Crypto Cellar researchers noted that Astra's two-day feat would typically take a human researcher weeks or even months to accomplish. They are currently analyzing logs to understand the exact methods and speed of Astra's decryption process.

Astra tackled the MVUEH message entirely on its own after being asked if it could break any of the unbroken Enigma messages on the Crypto Cellar Research page. It identified Nr. 172, MVUEH, as a promising target, suspecting a link to the plaintext of Nr. 173, SIPVX.

With its target set, and expecting the repeated place name "ROSENOW ROSENOW" as a probable plaintext clue, Astra developed Python and C++ software for an Enigma simulator and an Enigma Bombe. Its initial hunch proved correct, leading to the successful decryption.

The encrypted 82-letter MVUEH cipher began with "ICRVSORMCCWQTATYEVFXDBZGGSNXWLPSYWZYTCBSWULRTBZCVGODVJUSLSOOMJQJZSXSEBZPEYMDNXJYTC". Decrypted, it translates to: "Please specify the route of march. I am in Rosenow, Rosenow. Immediate reply by radio." A spelling mistake at the front of the original message added to the decoding challenge.

The Enigma machine featured a 26-key keyboard, a lampboard, and three rotors from a set of five, which advanced with every keypress. This complex mechanism meant that pressing the same letter repeatedly would produce a different encrypted output each time.

Further obfuscation was added by a plugboard, where operators could swap up to 10 letters using rerouting wires. To decode a message, one needed to know four daily-changing settings: rotor order, ring setting, rotor starting positions, and plugboard connections.

This is not GPT-Astra's first historical code-breaking achievement. Just last week, the LLM successfully deciphered a 108-year-old unsolved WWI German code that had been encrypted using the ADFGVX method.

headline_marked: [[Issabel Framework Hardcoded JWT Flaw]] (CVE-2026-89026) allows one key for every PBX
headline: Issabel Framework Hardcoded JWT Flaw (CVE-2026-89026) allows one key for every PBX
summary: The open-source Issabel Framework shipped with a critical hardcoded JWT signing key, enabling attackers to forge tokens and gain full code execution. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-89026) has a CVSS score of 9.8 and has seen active exploitation.
details: Issabel Framework, an open-source unified communications platform built around Asterisk, contained a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-89026) due to a hardcoded HS256 JWT signing key. This flaw, with a CVSS base score of 9.8, allowed attackers to forge valid bearer tokens for any installation. Exploitation was first observed on September 9, 2026, and public proof-of-concept code exists.

The pbxapi component, which validates these tokens, could be exploited to call the management originate function. This function passes a System parameter to Asterisk, executing arbitrary strings with Asterisk process privileges. No credentials or prior access are required, only network reach to the pbxapi endpoint.

Gaining code execution on the Asterisk host allows attackers to modify call routing for toll fraud, read recorded calls and voicemail, harvest extension credentials, and establish a foothold for lateral movement. While Asterisk often runs with low privileges, the initial access grants full code execution within the application context.

Users are urged to apply the upstream fix (commit b97dbaf) that removes the hardcoded key and rotate the signing secret on every instance. After upgrading, verify old tokens are rejected and restrict pbxapi access from untrusted networks.

Additionally, review call detail records for unusual activity, check for unexpected manager accounts, and confirm no scheduled tasks or web shells were left behind. If immediate upgrade is not possible, network-layer restriction of pbxapi access is crucial, as the flaw requires no user interaction and the endpoint is the entire attack surface.
